paragraphs: On Saturday morning, Lily sat next to a big window with Mia. Leo sat behind them with his small book. Teacher Kim sat in the front, next to the driver. A sign above her said, "PLEASE HOLD THE POLE." Another sign said, "GIVE YOUR SEAT TO OLDER PEOPLE." Many passengers sat together on the long blue seats.

After ten minutes, the driver went on the motorway. It was a long, straight road, and the traffic was fast. Cars and big trucks drove next to the bus. "How long is the ride?" asked Mia. "About half an hour," said Teacher Kim. A woman spoke from a speaker on the roof. "The next stop is the small zoo. Please press the red button." The woman repeated the message slowly. "I will press the button," said Lily.

Leo looked through the big window at the front of the bus. "It looks like a spaceship!" he said. He drew a long nose and round windows in his book. "Is it a fast spaceship?" asked Mia with a smile. "Yes, it is," said Leo. "It goes to a popular planet with many animals."

Lily pressed the red button. The driver stopped at a corner near the zoo. A short path went from the corner to the gate. The zoo is popular on Saturday, so many families walked there. "Please stay together," said Teacher Kim. She counted the children at the gate. Mia wanted to see the monkeys first. Lily wanted to take a photo of a tall giraffe.

Before they went in, Leo showed his picture to the driver. The driver smiled and said, "Nice spaceship!" "I like your picture," he said to Leo. Leo laughed and said, "Thank you!" "The next bus back is at half past twelve," said the driver. "Please be here on time."
text.summary: The Explorers ride to the small zoo on a Saturday morning. Signs and a voice on the way tell the reader where the children are, and Leo draws the bus as a spaceship.
